item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President presently organizes the NSC and Principals Committee, assigning their membership, attendance, leadership, meeting, and coordination functions; these are internal executive-management arrangements rather than changes to legal rights.","evidence":"I hereby direct that the National Security Council system be organized as follows."},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The National Security Advisor is assigned the ongoing internal task of setting the committee agenda after consultation, with no prescribed external legal consequence.","evidence":"The National Security Advisor shall determine the agenda in consultation with the other committee members"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The National Security Advisor must perform ongoing committee housekeeping and accurately report participants' views to the President; no legal consequence is imposed.","evidence":"shall ensure that necessary papers are prepared in advance and that conclusions and decisions are recorded and communicated in a timely manner"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"The segment presently structures the Deputies Committee and assigns its officials ongoing review, coordination, planning, meeting, and administrative responsibilities, without dictating a legally consequential agency outcome.","evidence":"The Deputies Committee (DC) shall review and monitor the work of the NSC interagency process"},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"The segment assigns the DC responsibility for decision-support papers and establishes IPCs as the internal mechanism for interagency policy coordination; these are organizational and analytical functions.","evidence":"The IPCs shall be the main day-to-day fora for interagency coordination of national security policy."},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The IPCs and National Security Advisor are assigned ongoing analysis, response, establishment, and chair-designation duties within the executive policymaking process, without a specified legal consequence.","evidence":"The IPCs shall be established at the direction of the National Security Advisor"},{"segment_id":"7","code":1,"rationale":"The segment internally organizes the NSC process by prescribing IPC operations and replacement of prior coordinating bodies, and by superseding earlier organizational guidance; these changes concern executive administration rather than substantive legal rights.","evidence":"This memorandum shall supersede all other existing Presidential guidance on the organization of the National Security Council system."}]}
